description: Crystallographic structure files for ZIF-8 (zeolitic imidazolate framework 8, Zn(2-methylimidazolate)2, sodalite topology). Target structure: cubic I-43m, a ~= 16.99 A, CSD refcode FAWCEN (Park et al. PNAS 2006). All files downloaded from the public internet on 2026-08-30; nothing was hand-edited. Verification (independent parse + full symmetry expansion with a numpy script): every file expands to the exact occupancy-weighted conventional-cell composition Zn12 C96 N48 H120 = 276 atoms.
verification_method: Custom CIF parser: extracted cell/space group/symmetry ops/atom sites, applied all symmetry operations to fractional coordinates, deduplicated positions (tol 1e-3 frac, periodic), summed occupancy-weighted counts per element. Expected Zn12 C96 N48 H120 per conventional cell; all three files match exactly.

files.publication: Shekhah, Swaidan, Belmabkhout, du Plessis, Jacobs, Barbour, Pinnau, Eddaoudi, 'The liquid phase epitaxy approach for the successful construction of ultra-thin and defect-free ZIF-8 membranes: pure and mixed gas transport study', Chem. Commun. 50, 2089 (2014), DOI 10.1039/c3cc47495j
files.structure_note: Guest-free (evacuated) ZIF-8 single crystal at 298 K, data block name ZIF8Vacuum. Independent redetermination of the FAWCEN framework, not the FAWCEN deposit itself.
files.hydrogen_note: H positions geometric (calc); methyl H3A/H3B/H3C have occupancy 0.5 (methyl rotor disordered across the crystallographic mirror, standard for ZIF-8 in I-43m). Occupancy-weighted expansion gives exactly H120.

files.publication: De Zitter, Perl, Savko, Paley, Thom, Jeangerard, Brewster, Tissot, Serre, Shepard, 'Elucidating metal-organic framework structures using synchrotron serial crystallography', CrystEngComm 26, 5644-5654 (2024), DOI 10.1039/D4CE00735B
files.structure_note: ZIF-8 Zn(mim)2 by synchrotron serial crystallography at 100 K, data block zif8_sg229_unmerged_a_solventmask. Cell a = 16.99(4) A matches the FAWCEN value 16.991 A. File is large (538 KB) because it embeds unmerged reflection data after the structural block.
files.content: asymmetric unit + 48 symmetry operations (plus embedded reflection data)
files.hydrogen_note: H positions geometric (calc); methyl H00A/H00B/H00C occupancy 0.5 (mirror-disordered methyl). Occupancy-weighted expansion gives exactly H120.

files.database: GitHub, numat/RASPA2 repository (structures/mofs/cif/ZIF-8.cif); file authored by David Dubbeldam (RASPA author), audit date 2011-3-6
files.publication: Cites Park, Ni, Cote, Choi, Huang, Uribe-Romo, Chae, O'Keeffe, Yaghi, 'Exceptional chemical and thermal stability of zeolitic imidazolate frameworks', Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 103(27), 10186-10191 (2006), DOI 10.1073/pnas.0602439103 -- i.e. this is the FAWCEN structure (CSD refcode FAWCEN), as distributed with the RASPA simulation package
files.structure_note: Simulation-ready P1 full-conventional-cell version of FAWCEN: all 276 atoms listed explicitly with occupancy 1 (one ordered orientation chosen for each methyl group, so no partial occupancies). a = 16.991 A is the published FAWCEN cell. This is the file most commonly used for ZIF-8 molecular simulation.
files.content: full conventional cell in P1, 276 atoms, all occupancy 1
files.hydrogen_note: All 120 H present at full occupancy (ordered methyl orientation).

notes: The original FAWCEN CIF itself is deposited at CCDC (Park et al. PNAS 2006); CCDC downloads require an interactive request form, so it was not fetched directly. The RASPA2 file is the standard FAWCEN-derived cell (a = 16.991 A) and the two COD entries are independent experimental redeterminations of the same framework.

Entries deliberately NOT used: COD 4118891/4118892 (SALEM-2, unsubstituted imidazolate, not 2-methylimidazolate), 4128140 (Fe analogue MUV-3), 7236367 (Zn/Co mixed), 7111968-7111972 (gas-loaded frameworks with guest electron density), 7243939 (electron-diffraction cell a=17.497 A, off the accepted value).
Verification script: parse + symmetry expansion, archived at scratchpad verify_cif.py during the session; results reproduced in this file.
